Induction Circuit Stability Under Fine-Tuning A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
threats.detail: Indexing errors, arbitrary thresholds, saturation, or nonlinear/discrete metrics can create misleading component scores or rankings.
threats.ruled_out_by: Validate the scoring implementation against an independent causal measure, report raw scores rather than thresholded membership alone, and compare with a continuous complementary metric.

SynthSAEBench: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Scalable Realistic Synthetic Data
threats.detail: Variant rankings may reflect training randomness or checkpoint jitter rather than architecture or training changes.
threats.ruled_out_by: Use multiple training seeds and post-warmup snapshots, decompose variance into variant, seed, and snapshot components, and report uncertainty.

threats.ruled_out_by: Compare with a bias control matched on correct agreement, inspect the ablation paths, and compare model and circuit component behavior and exact error agreement.

evidence: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data
Induction Circuit Stability Under Fine-Tuning A Mechanistic Interpretability Study

evidence_standards.detail: Use and report repeated seeds where available: examples include three seeds with mean ± SD or standard error, and five seeds with mean and standard deviation. State when the seed count is modest; do not imply a formal significance test where none was run.

evidence: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark

One induction-score study prespecifies a meaningful change of at least 0.1; one circuit-discovery comparison uses p<0.05 and reports Vargha–Delaney A12 effect size.

State the resampling unit and whether comparisons are paired. Where using paired-bootstrap significance testing, report the threshold (p<0.05) and describe nonsignificant comparisons as ties only under the stated procedure.

From Circuit Evidence to Mechanistic Theory: An Inductive Logic Approach

datasets.name: IOI
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-recovery task against the previously reported circuit; the task uses logit difference in prior work. ACDC and SP optimize KL divergence except where task-specific metrics are used in the metric ablation. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; split and trial count are not stated.

datasets.name: Docstring
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-recovery task against the previously reported circuit; the task uses logit difference in prior work. The paper also reports ACDC performance using the docstring metric. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; split and trial count are not stated.

datasets.name: Greater-Than
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-recovery task against the previously reported circuit; the task uses probability difference in prior work. ACDC and SP optimize KL divergence except where task-specific metrics are used in the metric ablation. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; split and trial count are not stated.

datasets.name: tracr-xproportion
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-recovery task against the previously reported circuit using mean squared error in prior work; the paper uses L2 distance rather than KL divergence for tracr tasks. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; split and trial count are not stated.

datasets.name: tracr-reverse
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-recovery task against the previously reported circuit using mean squared error in prior work; the paper uses L2 distance rather than KL divergence for tracr tasks. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; split and trial count are not stated.

datasets.name: Induction
datasets.eval_protocol: Circuit-recovery methods are evaluated by KL divergence from the original model on a held-out test set, alongside the number of circuit edges. The task-specific metric is negative log-probability; the paper also measures that metric for subgraphs recovered by optimizing KL divergence. Clean prompts are paired with corrupted prompts for activation patching; trial count is not stated.

baselines.name: Subnetwork Probing (SP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same circuit-recovery tasks and corrupted-data setup as ACDC; SP is modified to remove its linear probe, optimize KL divergence (or L2 distance for tracr tasks), and interpolate between corrupted and clean activations. Results are also compared under zero-activation patching.

baselines.name: Head Importance Score for Pruning (HISP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same circuit-recovery tasks; the paper generalizes HISP to replace heads and other components with corrupted activations. It is evaluated over the range of k values, keeping the top-k heads. Results are also compared under zero-activation patching.

metrics.name: ROC-AUC
metrics.caveat: The edge-level reference circuits are practitioner-reported and may contain extraneous edges or omit important ones, so AUC against them is an imperfect measure of recovery; the paper also plots TPR and FPR across thresholds, regularization values, or k.

metrics.name: TPR and FPR
metrics.caveat: These rates depend on the completeness and correctness of the practitioner-reported reference circuits; the paper reports them across operating points and summarizes performance with ROC-AUC.

metrics.name: KL divergence
metrics.caveat: It is an indirect measure of whether a circuit captures the behavior and does not rely on the completeness of prior circuits; the paper reports edge count alongside it and also checks the task-specific induction loss.

metrics.name: Number of edges
metrics.caveat: Fewer edges alone do not establish that a circuit captures the behavior; the paper reports it alongside KL divergence, with lower KL and fewer edges treated as better.

metrics.name: Logit difference
metrics.caveat: The paper notes that optimizing a single metric can miss components that are harmful to task performance, including negative components; it also evaluates circuit recovery using KL divergence.

metrics.name: Probability difference
metrics.caveat: The paper notes that optimizing a single metric can miss components that are harmful to task performance; it also evaluates circuit recovery using KL divergence.

metrics.name: Mean squared error (L2 distance)
metrics.caveat: The paper reports sensitivity to metric choice and uses L2 distance for tracr tasks rather than KL divergence; it does not state a further metric-specific caveat.

metrics.name: Negative log-probability (induction loss)
metrics.caveat: It is task-specific; the paper also reports KL divergence and edge count for the recovered subgraphs.

controls.name: Zero-activation patching
controls.detail: Alongside interchange patching with corrupted activations, the paper compares experiments that replace activations with zeros; the induction comparison reports both conditions.
controls.rules_out: Whether the reported recovery result depends on using corrupted activations rather than zero activations; it does not by itself establish that either patching choice is free of artifacts.

controls.name: Reset networks
controls.detail: Appendix L evaluates the methods on reset networks as well as trained networks, measuring KL divergence; the reset procedure is not specified in the provided text.
controls.rules_out: Whether methods find low-KL circuits even when the trained network’s induction behavior is absent; the paper reports that trained networks achieve significantly lower KL, while some methods also optimize the reset network.

confounds.name: The recovered subgraph may reflect an arbitrary or nonexistent circuit rather than the trained model’s task behavior
confounds.detail: A method could obtain apparently good circuit-recovery results even when the target behavior is not implemented by the network.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Appendix L compares KL divergence for trained networks and reset networks; trained networks achieve significantly lower KL, though the paper notes that SP and HISP can also optimize the reset network.

confounds.name: Recovery scores may depend on the corrupted activation distribution or metric choice rather than robustly identifying the circuit
confounds.detail: The paper reports that methods are very sensitive to the corrupted distribution and that performance varies with the metric and setup.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper experiments with different activation-patching and metric choices in Appendix E, and compares zero activations with corrupted activations; these experiments reveal sensitivity rather than ruling it out.

confounds.name: The reported ground-truth circuits may be incomplete or contain extraneous edges
confounds.detail: Practitioner-reported circuits used for ROC evaluation may omit important edges or include edges that are not necessary, making apparent false-positive or true-positive performance misleading.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper also evaluates induction circuits using KL divergence on a held-out test set and edge count, without relying on a prior circuit; it does not provide an independent validation of the reference circuits.

confounds.name: A method may miss circuit components that harm the chosen task metric
confounds.detail: Because the methods optimize a single metric, components that are actively harmful to task performance, such as negative components, may be omitted even if they belong to the circuit.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper examines recovery under KL divergence as well as task-specific metrics and reports that negative IOI components are recovered only at very small thresholds under KL, and not when optimizing logit difference; the limitation is not fully ruled out.

evidence_standards.name: ROC operating-point sweep and AUC
evidence_standards.detail: The paper sweeps ACDC thresholds, SP regularization parameters, and HISP pruning values; it plots TPR against FPR, uses pessimistic segments between Pareto-frontier points, and compares methods by ROC-AUC. No seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical test are stated.

evidence_standards.name: Held-out induction evaluation
evidence_standards.detail: For induction, the paper reports KL divergence on a held-out test set together with edge count, treating lower KL and fewer edges as better. It describes ACDC as having a slight advantage above 20 edges; no statistical test, variance estimate, or seed count is stated.

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k
datasets.eval_protocol: Toy ViT classification is reported with Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy; the evaluation split and item count are not stated. SAEs are trained on ImageNet-1k for one epoch, but the SAE evaluation split is not stated.

metrics.name: L0 (average active SAE latents per token)
metrics.caveat: The paper says L0 should be considered alongside explained variance; comparisons across vision and language can also be affected by patch/token granularity and token type.

metrics.name: Cross-entropy (CE)
metrics.caveat: SAE reconstruction can sometimes lower CE relative to the original model; the mechanism is unclear, with denoising proposed as a possible explanation. The paper also reports reconstruction CE and zero-ablation CE.

metrics.name: Reconstruction CE
metrics.caveat: It can be lower than the original CE; the paper says the mechanism is unclear and proposes denoising as a possible explanation.

metrics.name: Percentage of CE recovered
metrics.caveat: Reported values can exceed 100%; the paper does not state a caveat.

controls.name: Original model without SAE reconstruction
controls.detail: The tables report the original model CE alongside CE after injecting SAE reconstructions.
controls.rules_out: A lower reconstruction CE is a change relative to the unmodified model, rather than simply the model's original CE.

controls.name: Zero ablation
controls.detail: The tables report CE after zero-ablating activations alongside original and reconstruction CE.
controls.rules_out: Shows the loss under removal of the activations, providing a reference for interpreting reconstruction CE.

metrics.name: Logit difference / logprob difference
metrics.caveat: Can look better because the incorrect answer gets worse, including from indiscriminate damage to the model; inspect the individual answers’ logits or logprobs alongside it. It also ignores components that affect all compared logits.

metrics.name: Logprob
metrics.caveat: Can saturate after the correct answer becomes the top guess; is unspecific about changes to competing answers and can rise by inhibiting other top logits rather than increasing the correct-answer logit. Compare with logit difference or inspect individual logits.

metrics.name: Probability
metrics.caveat: Is nonlinear in logits, so the same logit change can produce very different probability changes; it also inherits logprob’s saturation and unspecificity. Compare with a continuous, roughly linear-in-logits metric such as logit difference or logprob.

metrics.name: Accuracy / top-k performance / rank
metrics.caveat: Discrete thresholds can hide meaningful partial contributions or make one component look decisive merely because it crosses a threshold. The paper recommends continuous metrics for exploratory patching; these discrete metrics can fit confirmatory patching.

metrics.name: Logits
metrics.caveat: Have an arbitrary baseline and can pick up components that contribute to many logits. Ensuring the residual stream and logits have mean zero can help address this.

metrics.name: KL divergence
metrics.caveat: Compares the full output and penalizes any deviation, but can track variation that may not matter for the task.

confounds.name: A logit-difference gain comes from worsening the incorrect answer rather than improving the correct answer
confounds.detail: Because the metric subtracts the incorrect-answer logit, indiscriminate damage that moves the model toward a uniform output can boost the difference.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Check the individual answers’ logits or logprobs alongside the difference.

confounds.name: A positive patching result tracks an incidental difference between the clean and corrupt prompts, not the hypothesized circuit property
confounds.detail: Patching is sensitive to which prompt properties change and supports claims only for the prompt distributions used.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use narrow prompt variations to isolate properties during exploration, and a wide distribution varying the hypothesized circuit’s variables for confirmation; the paper also recommends testing multiple corrupt prompt distributions where needed.

datasets.name: Indirect Object Identification (IOI)
datasets.eval_protocol: 40,000 generated instances; each name is a single token for all tested models. The private test set uses names and direct objects absent from the public train and test sets. Original-to-counterfactual mappings are fixed. Circuit localization is evaluated with CPR/CMD; causal-variable localization on GPT-2 uses mean-squared error between causal-model and model logits.

datasets.name: Arithmetic
datasets.eval_protocol: About 75,000 instances from enumerated one- and two-digit operand pairs for addition and subtraction, with six natural-language templates per pair. Original-to-counterfactual mappings are fixed. Circuit localization reports CPR/CMD; the causal-variable track evaluates the carry variable on two-digit addition using interchange intervention accuracy. Gemma-2 and Qwen-2.5 are omitted from arithmetic circuit evaluation because of their number tokenization.

datasets.name: Multiple-choice question answering (MCQA)
datasets.eval_protocol: 260 synthetic instances; every question has four choices and prompt-contained information. Fixed counterfactuals change answer position, choice letters, or both. Causal-variable localization reports interchange intervention accuracy; circuit localization reports CPR/CMD.

datasets.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses the original Easy and Challenge partitions (5,000 and 2,500 instances), analyzed separately, with the original four-choice prompt format. Fixed counterfactuals may change answer symbols or answer order. Circuit localization reports CPR/CMD; the causal-variable results shown are for ARC Easy and use interchange intervention accuracy.

datasets.name: RAVEL
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses the split for disentangling city country, continent, and language attributes. Half of the counterfactual prompts query a different attribute and half are random Wikipedia sentences containing the city; base prompts are balanced so half query the intervened attribute. Reports interchange intervention accuracy.

datasets.name: InterpBench
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses an IOI model implementing a known ground-truth circuit; circuit localization is scored by AUROC over edges.

baselines.name: Edge activation patching (EActP, CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated against other circuit-localization methods on the same tasks and models where tractable, using the paper's circuit-size and faithfulness metrics. The paper notes EActP used fewer examples in some evaluations because of runtime.

baselines.name: Edge Attribution Patching (EAP, CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Methods are assigned importance scores to edges or nodes and evaluated using top-scoring components or greedy search, with circuit size and faithfulness measured by the benchmark protocol.

baselines.name: EAP (mean ablations)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; uses mean ablations rather than counterfactual ablations.

baselines.name: EAP (optimal ablations, OA)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; the OA ablation vectors are optimized to minimize expected task-dataset cross-entropy loss.

baselines.name: EAP-IG-inputs (CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; uses five integrated-gradient steps.

baselines.name: EAP-IG-activations (CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; uses five integrated-gradient steps.

baselines.name: Node Attribution Patching (NAP, CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol.

baselines.name: NAP-IG (CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; uses five integrated-gradient steps.

baselines.name: Information Flow Routes (IFR)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol; adapted to the paper's circuit formalization.

baselines.name: Uniform Gradient Sampling (UGS, CF)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with other circuit-localization methods using the benchmark circuit-size and faithfulness protocol.

baselines.name: Full Vector
baselines.fair_comparison: Causal-variable baseline using the identity featurizer and all dimensions of the untransformed hidden vector; evaluated with the same task counterfactuals and interchange-intervention protocol as other feature-alignment methods.

baselines.name: DBM
baselines.fair_comparison: Learns a binary feature mask with high-level causal-model supervision to maximize training-set faithfulness; evaluated on the same task counterfactuals as the other causal-variable methods.

baselines.name: DBM + PCA
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses PCA features with DBM feature selection; trained and evaluated under the same causal-variable task protocol as the other methods.

baselines.name: DBM + SAE
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses GemmaScope or LlamaScope SAE features with DBM feature selection; evaluated under the same causal-variable task protocol as the other methods.

baselines.name: Distributed Alignment Search (DAS)
baselines.fair_comparison: Learns features with high-level causal-model supervision to maximize faithfulness; evaluated on the same task counterfactuals as the other causal-variable methods.

metrics.name: Circuit Performance Ratio (CPR)
metrics.caveat: Faithfulness can conflate finding components that positively affect task performance with finding components that have any strong effect. CPR isolates the positive-performance goal; the paper reports CMD alongside it for the broader-effect goal.

metrics.name: Circuit-Model Distance (CMD)
metrics.caveat: Faithfulness can conflate positive contributions with any measurable impact, including negative impact. CMD captures deviation from the full model across circuit sizes; the paper reports CPR alongside it to measure positive-performance recovery.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.caveat: Used on the ground-truth-circuit InterpBench model because realistic-model CPR/CMD best- and worst-case values cannot be anticipated without a known circuit; AUROC over edges is reported instead.

metrics.name: Interchange intervention accuracy (IIA)
metrics.caveat: The paper filters out examples where the model predicts incorrectly on the base input or any counterfactual, so the score measures alignment only on examples the model handles correctly.

metrics.name: Mean-squared error (IOI causal-variable track)
metrics.caveat: For IOI, the paper uses a logit-based metric rather than token-level interchange intervention accuracy; it reports MSE between causal-model and deep-learning-model logits.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.caveat: The paper reports 0-shot greedy-generation task performance to establish model capability, and also refers to ranked-choice scoring in the appendix; it does not specify a further caveat for accuracy.

controls.name: Random circuits
controls.detail: Uniformly sample an importance score in [-1,1] for every model edge; report mean CPR and CMD across three random seeds.
controls.rules_out: Provides a sanity-check reference for whether discovered circuits outperform randomly selected circuits under the benchmark metrics.

confounds.name: EActP's weaker results may be due to fewer evaluation examples rather than method quality
confounds.detail: The authors say they used fewer examples for EActP because exact edge activation patching is slow; this could explain its lower scores in some comparisons.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out in the reported evaluation; the paper identifies reduced example count as a possible explanation.

confounds.name: Independent edge-effect estimates may not predict joint effects of ablating multiple edges
confounds.detail: EActP and attribution methods estimate component effects independently, which may imperfectly predict the effect of ablating several edges together.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper compares with UGS, which considers many edges at once, but notes that UGS is also not the top performer; it does not establish that independent-effect estimation is harmless.

confounds.name: DAS's advantage may come from supervision rather than its learned feature representation alone
confounds.detail: The authors note DAS is the only causal-variable baseline that learns features with supervision from the high-level causal model.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out by a supervision-matched comparison; the paper presents DAS's supervised status as an explanation for its stronger results.

confounds.name: Weak arithmetic results may reflect tokenization or a non-linear carry representation, rather than absence of a carry variable
confounds.detail: The authors suggest Gemma-2's results may relate to its digit-by-digit tokenization, while the carry variable might instead be represented in a non-linear feature space.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports model tokenization and carry-localization results, but says the results leave these alternatives open.

confounds.name: The apparent weakness of PCA on MCQA may reflect its low-data regime rather than PCA generally
confounds.detail: The authors suspect that the approximately 100 training examples used for MCQA impair the quality of the computed principal components.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out; the paper offers this as a suspected explanation and reports no separate higher-data comparison.

confounds.name: Baseline rankings may reflect incomplete hyperparameter tuning
confounds.detail: The authors concede that they did not conduct exhaustive hyperparameter searches for any causal-variable baseline.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out; the paper identifies this as a limitation and says the tasks may have room for improvement.

evidence_standards.name: Random-circuit results averaged over 3 seeds
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reports mean CPR and CMD across three random seeds for its random-circuit sanity check; it specifies no significance test or minimum effect size.

evidence_standards.name: 0-shot greedy-generation setting
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reports the model-capability results in Table 1 using 0-shot prompts and greedy decoding.

evidence_standards.name: Averaging across counterfactual datasets and layers, with best-layer results also shown
evidence_standards.detail: For causal-variable localization, the paper reports the mean across counterfactual datasets and layers and, separately, the best alignment across layers. It specifies no statistical test or margin for declaring differences real.

datasets.name: Indirect-object identification (IOI)
datasets.eval_protocol: Held-out evaluation prompts; score is the logit difference between the correct and counterfactual tokens. Within-prompt experiments use 256 exact measurements per layer; across-prompt experiments use B ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128} heads per prompt, with calibration on separate prompts of the same task.

datasets.name: Factual completion
datasets.eval_protocol: Held-out evaluation prompts; score is the logit difference between the correct and counterfactual tokens. Within-prompt experiments use 256 exact measurements per layer; across-prompt experiments use B ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128} heads per prompt, with calibration on separate prompts of the same task. Dataset-average correction is evaluated without exact measurements on the evaluation prompts.

datasets.name: Subject-verb agreement (SVA)
datasets.eval_protocol: Held-out evaluation prompts; score is the logit difference between the correct and counterfactual tokens. Within-prompt experiments use 256 exact measurements per layer; across-prompt experiments use B ∈ {16, 32, 64, 128} heads per prompt, with calibration on separate prompts of the same task.

baselines.name: verify-more
baselines.fair_comparison: Spends the same measurement budget on exact AP for components with the largest AtP magnitudes and leaves the rest uncorrected. Comparisons are runtime-matched within prompts or matched in projected total cost across prompts, including calibration.

baselines.name: ProbeCal
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses randomized Hessian-diagonal curvature-probe sketches instead of exact calibration labels; compared with verify-more at matched projected total cost, including calibration.

baselines.name: AtP / uncorrected AtP averages
baselines.fair_comparison: Dataset-average corrections are compared with uncorrected AtP without exact measurements on the evaluation prompts.

baselines.name: verify-more on AtP∗ estimates
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on Gemma-2-9B; the paper does not state further matching details.

baselines.name: selective HVP
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the 30-group Gemma comparison set at the tested settings; no further matching details are stated.

baselines.name: MS-HVP
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the 30-group Gemma comparison set at the tested settings; no further matching details are stated.

baselines.name: singleton IG
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the 30-group Gemma comparison set at the tested settings; no further matching details are stated.

baselines.name: exhaustive AP
baselines.fair_comparison: Provides exact effects but at greater cost; no further matching details are stated.

baselines.name: direct averaging of the same AP effects
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with residual correction using the same AP measurements.

metrics.name: Per-prompt effect-vector MAE
metrics.caveat: Lower MAE need not improve top-ten recall; low effect-vector error also does not establish faithfulness of a jointly intervened circuit.

metrics.name: Relative AP error
metrics.reported_alongside: Summed absolute error divided by summed absolute effects.

metrics.name: Dataset-average error / MAE
metrics.caveat: Signed error transfer can fail: the paper reports a 52% MAE increase for Guided-AP on Qwen2.5 IOI, and no established dataset-average correction gain for SVA.
metrics.reported_alongside: Compared with uncorrected AtP; dataset-average recall gain is not established.

metrics.name: Recall of the ten largest effects
metrics.caveat: Lower MAE need not improve this metric.
metrics.reported_alongside: Reported alongside MAE; top-ten recall remains nearly perfect for both within-prompt methods.

metrics.name: Warm runtime and projected cost
metrics.caveat: Costs depend on task, measurement budget, hardware, and implementation; the paper distinguishes measured within-prompt warm runtime from projected calibration-plus-deployment cost across prompts.
metrics.reported_alongside: Warm runtime is reported per layer; across-prompt projections include calibration and fitting costs.

metrics.name: Error reduction
metrics.reported_alongside: Defined as one minus the ratio of mean errors.

controls.name: verify only
controls.detail: Uses the measurement budget for verification without correction; compared with within-prompt Guided-AP at the same 256-measurement budget.
controls.rules_out: Whether correction improves estimates beyond spending the budget on verification alone.

controls.name: verify + shift using verification measurements
controls.detail: Shifts the remaining estimates by the median residual of the components chosen for verification; tested at the same 256-measurement budget.
controls.rules_out: Whether the gain comes merely from applying a shift estimated from measured components, rather than from the representative pilot. This control raises MAE in eight of nine settings.

controls.name: mean rather than median pilot correction
controls.detail: Uses the mean residual instead of the median on identical pilot labels.
controls.rules_out: Whether the reported correction gain is specific to the median; the median performs better in all nine tested settings.

controls.name: direct averaging of the same AP effects
controls.detail: Uses the same AP measurements as average effects instead of learning residual corrections.
controls.rules_out: Whether average-correction gains come simply from reusing exact AP measurements; direct averaging has 5.8 to 14.9 times more error in the reported settings.

confounds.name: The apparent gain could come from shifting estimates using measurements that are not representative of the unmeasured components.
confounds.detail: A shift based on the verification-selected components could appear to help without the pilot capturing a shared error pattern.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper tests a verify-plus-shift control using the median residual of verification measurements; it raises MAE in eight of nine settings, while the representative-pilot method improves over the better of that control and verification alone.

confounds.name: Dataset-average gains could come from directly averaging measured AP effects rather than modeling recurring attribution errors.
confounds.detail: The same exact measurements might improve averages without the claimed residual-correction mechanism.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper compares residual correction with direct averaging of the same AP effects; direct averaging yields 5.8 to 14.9 times more error in every reported setting.

confounds.name: Across-prompt corrections may transfer biased or unrepresentative residuals because of selection bias.
confounds.detail: A learned signed correction could increase error if calibration residuals do not represent the evaluation prompts.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out generally: the paper reports a 52% increase in Qwen2.5 IOI dataset-average MAE, consistent with selection bias, and notes that correction can mislead when labels are not representative.

evidence_standards.name: Paired group bootstrap intervals
evidence_standards.detail: Intervals use paired group bootstraps; they are adjusted over the prespecified across-prompt comparison family and are descriptive for within-prompt comparisons. The paper does not specify a seed count, a separate statistical-test name, or a numerical no-difference margin.

datasets.name: Indirect Object Identification (IOI)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-discovery task using GPT-2, attn-4l, and redwood-2l. Edge-classification AUC-ROC uses 21 thresholds logarithmically evenly spaced from 0.001 to 3.16, consistent with ACDC; task and KL-divergence metrics are also reported. Runtime and memory comparisons use threshold 0.001.

datasets.name: Greater Than
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-discovery task using GPT-2, attn-4l, and redwood-2l. Edge-classification AUC-ROC uses 21 thresholds logarithmically evenly spaced from 0.001 to 3.16, consistent with ACDC; task and KL-divergence metrics are also reported.

datasets.name: Docstring
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluated as a circuit-discovery task using GPT-2, attn-4l, and redwood-2l. Edge-classification AUC-ROC uses 21 thresholds logarithmically evenly spaced from 0.001 to 3.16, consistent with ACDC; task and KL-divergence metrics are also reported.

controls.name: ACDC without PAHQ
controls.detail: The original, unaccelerated ACDC is evaluated alongside PAHQ-accelerated ACDC.
controls.rules_out: Provides an unmodified reference for comparing faithfulness, runtime, and memory.

controls.name: Weight-loading stream only
controls.detail: In the GPT-2 IOI scheduler ablation, enable the weight-loading stream and disable the low/high-precision computation stream; runtime is 49 minutes.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether the runtime improvement can be attributed to weight-loading-stream scheduling alone.

controls.name: Low/high-precision computation stream only
controls.detail: In the GPT-2 IOI scheduler ablation, disable the weight-loading stream and enable the low/high-precision computation stream; runtime is 72 minutes.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether the runtime improvement can be attributed to computation-stream scheduling alone.

controls.name: Neither scheduler stream enabled
controls.detail: In the GPT-2 IOI scheduler ablation, disable both streams; runtime is 94 minutes.
controls.rules_out: Provides the no-scheduler reference for the scheduler ablation.

confounds.name: The selected edge’s high-precision signal may degrade in downstream layers that use lower precision
confounds.detail: If downstream low-precision computation erased the patched signal, the method’s claimed faithfulness could be compromised even when the selected component itself is computed at high precision.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports empirical faithfulness measurements, including AUC-ROC and task/KL-divergence results across IOI, Greater Than, and Docstring, and reports PAHQ close to original ACDC. The authors acknowledge this is empirical support rather than a full theoretical resolution.

datasets.name: Toy model of equivariant features
datasets.eval_protocol: Synthetic inputs are sums of independently active ground-truth features, each active with probability 1/N; D=16 and N=8, 16, 18, or 32. The main figure uses orbit size 4; results are also reported for orbit sizes 8, 16, and 32 in the appendix. Evaluate feature-detection accuracy using the top-m candidate SAE latents, mean cosine similarity for feature recovery, and reconstruction MSE. No split or sample count is stated.

datasets.name: Shapes
datasets.eval_protocol: Synthetic images contain 4 of 8 possible shapes in 4 positions; evaluate under C4 rotations and D4 rotations plus vertical flips. Construct 180 binary tasks covering shape, shape-position, shape-orientation, and shape-position-orientation. Filter latents by maximum absolute difference between classes and train XGBoost probes on filtered latents and M-transformed reconstructions. Report probe F1, averaged over the four task types and three seeds in the cited figure. No split or episode count is stated.

datasets.name: GalaxyMNIST
datasets.eval_protocol: Use 10,000 galaxy images over 4 invariant classes and evaluate under C4 and D4 symmetries. For 4-way galaxy-morphology classification, filter SAE latents by highest between-class variance and train logistic probes on average channel vectors per image; probes use SAE latents because labels are invariant to C4 and D4. No split or episode count is stated.

datasets.name: MLL23
datasets.eval_protocol: Use 41,906 peripheral-blood single-cell images with 18 cell types and evaluate under C4 and D4 symmetries. For 18-way cell-type classification, filter SAE latents by highest between-class variance and train logistic probes; probes use SAE latents because labels are invariant to C4 and D4. No split or episode count is stated.

baselines.name: Vanilla TopK SAE, narrow
baselines.fair_comparison: Same number of latents as the Equivariant SAEs; SAEs use the same two-layer encoder module and are trained on augmented data.

baselines.name: Vanilla TopK SAE, wide
baselines.fair_comparison: Four times as many latents as the Equivariant SAEs; SAEs use the same two-layer encoder module and are trained on augmented data.

baselines.name: Archetypal TopK SAE, narrow
baselines.fair_comparison: Same number of latents as the Equivariant SAEs; SAEs use the same two-layer encoder module and are trained on augmented data.

baselines.name: Archetypal TopK SAE, wide
baselines.fair_comparison: Four times as many latents as the Equivariant SAEs; SAEs use the same two-layer encoder module and are trained on augmented data.

baselines.name: Group crosscoder
baselines.fair_comparison: Trained on augmented data. It uses |G| blocks per feature to model transformations; the paper does not state a further matching of capacity or hyperparameters.

metrics.name: Feature-detection accuracy
metrics.caveat: Reconstruction quality alone can be misleading about feature usefulness; on the toy model the paper also evaluates feature recovery and reconstruction error.

metrics.name: Reconstruction error (MSE)
metrics.caveat: The paper finds reconstruction quality can be inversely correlated with feature usefulness and says it should not be relied on as the primary interpretability measure; it reports probing performance and, on the toy model, feature recovery and detection alongside it.

metrics.name: Normalized reconstruction MSE
metrics.caveat: The paper cautions that reconstruction quality can be inversely correlated with feature usefulness; it reports probing performance alongside reconstruction results.

metrics.name: Base-model MSE when the SAE is substituted into the model
metrics.caveat: The paper cautions that reconstruction quality can be inversely correlated with feature usefulness; it reports probing performance alongside reconstruction results.

metrics.name: Probe accuracy
metrics.caveat: The paper does not claim probing over SAE latents or outputs is the optimal classification approach, and notes probing over base-model activations can perform better.

metrics.name: Probe F1 score
metrics.caveat: The paper does not claim probing over SAE latents or outputs is the optimal classification approach, and notes probing over base-model activations can perform better.

metrics.name: R² for predicting transformed activations
metrics.caveat: The paper reports the identity-transformation baseline (M=I) alongside learned-transformation R² scores.

controls.name: Identity transformation (M=I)
controls.detail: For predicting transformed activations, compare the learned transformation against setting M to the identity matrix.
controls.rules_out: That the learned transformation’s prediction performance is explained simply by activations already being invariant to the input transformations.

confounds.name: Non-equivariant SAEs reconstruct disparate inputs using features that do not align with ground-truth features
confounds.detail: This could explain why their reconstructions look good without their learned features capturing the semantic features of interest.
confounds.ruled_out_by: On the toy model, evaluate feature recovery by mean cosine similarity to ground-truth features and feature detection by classification accuracy, in addition to reconstruction error.

evidence_standards.name: Three random seeds; report means and standard errors
evidence_standards.detail: The paper states that all results are averaged over three random seeds and figures show standard errors. It does not specify a statistical test or a numerical threshold for treating differences as real.

datasets.name: Indirect object identification (IOI)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluates recovered circuits against the manually discovered circuit using ROC AUC while sweeping CD-T node-selection percentiles from 90 to 99; also reports faithfulness averaged over the dataset, with faithfulness defined relative to the all-heads-ablated model and the full model. No split or task-specific sample count is stated in the provided text.

datasets.name: Greater-than
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluates recovered circuits against the manually discovered circuit using ROC AUC while sweeping CD-T node-selection percentiles from 90 to 99; also reports faithfulness averaged over the dataset, with faithfulness defined relative to the all-heads-ablated model and the full model. No split or task-specific sample count is stated in the provided text.

datasets.name: Docstring completion (Docstring)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluates recovered circuits against the manually discovered circuit using ROC AUC while sweeping CD-T node-selection percentiles from 90 to 99; also reports faithfulness averaged over the dataset, with faithfulness defined relative to the all-heads-ablated model and the full model. No split or task-specific sample count is stated in the provided text.

baselines.name: ACDC
baselines.fair_comparison: Both baselines use node-level patching to match CD-T. The paper uses ACDC optimized for KL divergence rather than task-specific metrics.

baselines.name: EAP
baselines.fair_comparison: Both baselines use node-level patching to match CD-T.

metrics.name: ROC AUC
metrics.caveat: Uses manually discovered circuits as a reference, but the paper notes manual circuits are an imperfect reference standard because ground-truth circuits are lacking; faithfulness is also evaluated.

metrics.name: Faithfulness
metrics.caveat: Can exceed 1 when a circuit does not perfectly reproduce interactions between positively and negatively contributing heads; the paper reports comparisons to the full model and random circuits. Defined as (m(C)-m(∅))/(m(M)-m(∅)).

controls.name: Random circuits of the same size
controls.detail: Samples circuits from all possible nodes in the full model; the hypothesis-testing experiment repeats sampling 10 times. A separate size-growth comparison selects original-model attention heads in random order.
controls.rules_out: That CD-T circuit faithfulness is merely a lucky draw from the random-circuit reference distribution.

controls.name: Zero-ablation CD-T circuits
controls.detail: Compares faithfulness of CD-T circuits obtained with zero-ablation against circuits obtained with mean-ablation.
controls.rules_out: That the reported faithfulness comparison applies independently of the ablation choice; the paper reports mean-ablation tends to yield higher faithfulness on Greater-than and Docstring, while IOI is comparable.

controls.name: Full model
controls.detail: Measures task performance of the unablated model as the reference in the faithfulness calculation.
controls.rules_out: Provides the reference behavior that a circuit is claimed to replicate.

controls.name: All-heads-ablated corrupted model
controls.detail: Measures m(∅), the baseline performance when all heads are ablated, used in the faithfulness calculation.
controls.rules_out: Provides the no-specific-input-information baseline for the faithfulness calculation.

confounds.name: CD-T circuit faithfulness is due to random chance
confounds.detail: A small circuit might appear faithful simply by being a lucky selection of nodes, rather than because it preserves the model’s mechanism.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compares CD-T circuits with same-size random circuits sampled from all possible model nodes; reports the fraction q* of random circuits they outperform.

evidence_standards.name: Random-circuit hypothesis test
evidence_standards.detail: Samples random circuits 10 times and reports q*, the fraction of the same-size random-circuit reference distribution that the CD-T circuit is more faithful than; reported results include q*=0.8.

datasets.name: Base IOI
datasets.eval_protocol: GPT-2 small is evaluated on 200 generated prompts using the base IOI format; performance is scored by logit difference, the log probability of the IO token minus that of the S token. Prompts are constructed by sampling from template sentences and lists of names, places, and objects.

datasets.name: DoubleIO
datasets.eval_protocol: GPT-2 small and the base IOI circuit are evaluated on 200 generated prompts; the IO and S tokens are both duplicated. Performance is scored by logit difference, the log probability of the IO token minus that of the S token. Prompts are constructed by sampling from template sentences and lists of names, places, and objects.

datasets.name: TripleIO
datasets.eval_protocol: GPT-2 small and the base IOI circuit are evaluated on 200 generated prompts; the IO token appears three times and the S token twice. Performance is scored by logit difference, the log probability of the IO token minus that of the S token. Prompts are constructed by sampling from template sentences and lists of names, places, and objects.

baselines.name: GPT-2 small full model
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with circuits on the same prompt variants using logit difference; the circuit is evaluated as a subgraph of GPT-2 small.

baselines.name: Base IOI circuit (Wang et al., 2023)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with the DoubleIO and TripleIO circuits on the same prompt variants; the paper reports logit differences and circuit overlap.

metrics.name: Logit difference
metrics.caveat: A circuit can have a higher score than the full model without faithfully explaining its behavior; the paper reports circuit faithfulness alongside the model and circuit logit differences.

metrics.name: Faithfulness
metrics.caveat: A ratio far from 1, including values above 1, indicates that circuit performance does not align with full-model performance; the paper reports the underlying model and circuit logit differences alongside it.

metrics.name: Normalized faithfulness
metrics.caveat: Values far from the ideal value of 1 indicate a mismatch with full-model performance; the paper reports logit differences alongside it.

metrics.name: Confidence ratio
metrics.caveat: A ratio above 1 indicates more attention to the correct than the incorrect token, but the paper compares circuit and model ratios and also reports functional faithfulness to assess whether the circuit behaves like the model.

metrics.name: Functional faithfulness
metrics.caveat: A value near 1 indicates similar attention in circuit and model; values above or below 1 indicate behavioral differences. The paper reports confidence ratios alongside it.

controls.name: Unmodified GPT-2 small full model
controls.detail: The full model is evaluated alongside the circuit on the prompt variants using logit difference.
controls.rules_out: Whether the circuit’s performance matches or differs from the unmodified model’s behavior.

controls.name: Base IOI circuit with no restored extra input-token paths
controls.detail: The paper starts from the base IOI circuit and compares it with versions that restore paths from additional input tokens.
controls.rules_out: Whether performance changes are attributable to the added input paths rather than the base circuit alone.

controls.name: IO1-only and other-input-token path restorations
controls.detail: For DoubleIO, the paper tests adding paths from IO1 alone and from other input tokens, alongside adding paths from IO2; it reports that IO1 has little impact and other inputs further degrade performance.
controls.rules_out: That restoring arbitrary input paths explains the effect of restoring paths from the duplicated IO tokens.

confounds.name: S2 Hacking caused by the circuit knockout procedure, rather than the full model solving the variants through the claimed mechanism
confounds.detail: Mean-ablation of paths outside the base IOI circuit leaves S2 as the only input token with paths to the Duplicate Token and Induction heads, which can force suppression of subject tokens and produce high circuit scores without reflecting how the full model solves the task.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper does not rule this explanation out; it identifies and supports it by examining the mean-ablation paths and comparing model and circuit confidence ratios and functional faithfulness for heads 3.0, 5.5, 5.9, and 8.6.

confounds.name: Prompt order, rather than a prompt-order-independent mechanism, accounts for some DoubleIO performance
confounds.detail: The paper observes that performance differs depending on whether S or IO appears first, so aggregate performance could reflect the order distribution.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper stratifies logit differences by whether S or IO appears first and measures head 2.2’s attention to the corresponding name-plus-one token; these measurements show an order-sensitive, first-come-first-serve effect rather than ruling it out.

confounds.name: Circuit components change their behavior on the variants instead of being reused with their base IOI functions
confounds.detail: Similar overall circuit performance could occur even if component behavior changed under the new prompt formats.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper compares head attention patterns between base IOI and the variants, and measures head-level confidence ratios, functional faithfulness, and causal effects; it reports that most base-circuit components and heads are reused, while identifying deviations such as S2 Hacking.

evidence_standards.name: Confidence intervals based on 50 samples
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reports confidence intervals for the head-level confidence-ratio and functional-faithfulness metrics based on 50 samples; it does not state a statistical test, a significance threshold, a no-difference margin, or a seed-based rule.

datasets.name: IOI
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses the standard name-swap corruption and 50 templated prompts, with the indirect object (Mary) as the target; M is the log-probability of the correct next token. For circuit ranking, ranks all 144 GPT-2 Small attention heads and compares with activation-patching ground truth using top-k overlap and Spearman correlation.

datasets.name: Greater-Than
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses 200 prompts of the form “The war lasted from the year 17{XX} to the year 17”; corruption replaces the token at position 3 with a uniformly sampled vocabulary token. Measures whether the model assigns higher probability to years greater than XX. For GPT-2 Small, ranks all 144 attention heads and evaluates top-k overlap against activation-patching ground truth.

datasets.name: Factual completion
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses factual next-token prediction prompts and measures component-intervention effects on the correct-token log-probability; corruption replaces the token at position 3 with a uniformly sampled vocabulary token. Generic sweeps use 20 prompts unless otherwise noted; selected experiments use 55 prompts for Pythia-410M attention heads and 35 prompts for Qwen2.5-1.5B attention-head and MLP-output settings.

baselines.name: Attribution patching
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same prompts and component collections as the corresponding HVP experiments; activation-patching effects provide the ground truth for error measurement.

baselines.name: AtP*
baselines.fair_comparison: Reimplemented from the paper description because no official implementation was available; compared on matched prompt sets and component collections, with comparisons restricted to attention-head experiments.

baselines.name: GIM
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the public implementation with the softmax backward pass modified to remove the self-repair gradient term; evaluated on the same prompt sets and component collections as the corresponding HVP experiments.

baselines.name: Integrated Gradients (IG)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same tasks, including matched-compute comparisons; uses a per-component formulation with S interpolation steps and cost S per component.

baselines.name: Integrated Hessians (IH / IH-PI)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the evaluated tasks against HVP/MS-HVP; the paper reports comparisons at equal or higher computational cost.

baselines.name: Activation patching
baselines.fair_comparison: Used as the causal ground truth for component effects and rankings on the same evaluation inputs; its cost is reported as N×.

baselines.name: Local activation-curvature correction using f''(z)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with network-level curvature on the same patch direction; the paper reports the local-curvature correction’s error relative to making no correction.

baselines.name: Third-order Taylor expansion
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared in the pathological high-curvature Pythia-410M IOI setting; the paper reports that it fails catastrophically there.

baselines.name: Finite-difference HVP
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared in the pathological high-curvature Pythia-410M IOI setting; the paper reports that it fails catastrophically there.

baselines.name: Gauss–Newton correction
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared in the pathological high-curvature Pythia-410M IOI setting; the paper reports that it fails catastrophically there.

metrics.name: Top-5 relative error
metrics.caveat: Measures error only on the five components with largest activation-patching effect; the paper also reports circuit-ranking and recovery metrics. Defined as mean absolute score error normalized by the ground-truth score range.

metrics.name: Kendall tau
metrics.caveat: Global ranking correlations can understate gains at circuit-membership boundaries; the paper also reports recovery at the known circuit-size boundary and top-k overlap.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.caveat: Overall AUROC varies across models; the paper also reports AUROC stratified by perturbation magnitude and true-effect magnitude, plus precision and recall at specified reliability-score thresholds.

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.caveat: Reported alongside recall at the reliability-score threshold; at R̃>0.3, recall is 89% and precision is 36%.

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.caveat: Reported alongside precision at the reliability-score threshold; at R̃>0.3, recall is 89% and precision is 36%.

metrics.name: Computational cost
metrics.caveat: The paper reports both backward-pass cost and wall-clock runtime; IG becomes infeasible at 8B scale, so cost-matched comparisons are limited to feasible settings.

controls.name: Random component selection for selective HVP
controls.detail: Compares R̃-ranked component selection with a random baseline as more components are corrected; the comparison is shown against correction cost.
controls.rules_out: That the selective-workflow gains arise merely from correcting an arbitrary subset of components rather than selecting components using R̃.

confounds.name: Attribution-patching error is due to local activation curvature rather than downstream network response
confounds.detail: If true, local activation curvature should predict the relevant correction and account for the observed attribution-patching error.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measures network-level Hessian curvature against local activation curvature across three model families: network-level curvature is 2–66× larger with near-zero correlation (r=0.04); using f''(z) for correction produces >750% error.

confounds.name: Gains depend on synthetic token-replacement corruptions rather than structured perturbations
confounds.detail: If true, HVP’s error reduction would not carry over from random-token perturbations to semantically coherent activation changes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Tests cross-prompt resample and zero corruptions, and semantic entity-swap corruptions; HVP reduces error by 54% on GPT-2 and 59% on Pythia-410M under entity swaps.

confounds.name: Reported gains are driven by small evaluation samples
confounds.detail: If true, aggregate error-reduction estimates would change substantially as more evaluation prompts are included.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Varies evaluation sample size and reports that aggregate error-reduction estimates stabilize after approximately 10–15 prompts.

evidence_standards.name: 95% prompt-bootstrap confidence intervals
evidence_standards.detail: Uses 1,000 bootstrap resamples over prompts, sampling prompts with replacement and aggregating over all components in the sampled prompt set; reports the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles.

evidence_standards.name: Paired-bootstrap significance testing
evidence_standards.detail: Marks comparisons as significant at p<0.05. The paper describes nonsignificant comparisons as statistically tied in matched-compute results; it specifies no separate equivalence margin.

evidence_standards.name: Circuit-ranking results as point estimates
evidence_standards.detail: IOI and Greater-Than circuit-ranking metrics are reported as point estimates over the benchmark datasets.

datasets.name: OpenWebText
datasets.eval_protocol: SAEs are trained on GPT-2 hidden embeddings from over 80 million tokens. Norm and metric plots use 1,000 input sequences of length 128; the paper does not specify a split. Top-AFA comparisons use GPT-2 layers 6, 7, and 8.

baselines.name: top-k SAE
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on GPT-2 layers 6, 7, and 8 using h=16×d; the paper follows the experimental setup of Bussmann et al. (2024). No further matching details are stated.

baselines.name: batch top-k SAE
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on GPT-2 layers 6, 7, and 8 using h=16×d; the paper follows the experimental setup of Bussmann et al. (2024). Layer 8 also enables direct comparison with prior work. No further matching details are stated.

metrics.name: MSE (reconstruction loss)
metrics.caveat: Measures the relationship between the input embedding and its reconstruction, not the relationship between the input embedding and feature activations; the paper reports ε_LBO alongside it and finds differences in distributions and layer rankings.

metrics.name: NMSE (normalized MSE)
metrics.caveat: Like MSE, reflects reconstruction loss rather than the input-feature activation relationship; the paper reports ε_LBO alongside it, with differing distributions and rankings.

metrics.name: ε_LBO
metrics.caveat: Uses SAE-estimated feature activations because ground-truth activations are inaccessible; the paper reports NMSE alongside it and notes that the two metrics can rank layers differently.

metrics.name: Embedding and feature activation norms (‖z‖₂ and ‖f‖₂)

confounds.name: Top-AFA gains may depend on tuning the AFA-loss coefficient
confounds.detail: The paper acknowledges that Top-AFA's effectiveness depends on proper tuning of λ_AFA, so the result may depend on that training-time choice.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Appendix I reports that a coefficient of 1/16 was stable across the tested layers; the paper does not claim this removes the need for tuning.

datasets.name: IOI
datasets.eval_protocol: Generate prompts from 15 template families in ABBA and BABA order, sampling distinct single-token names and filling place and object slots from library vocabularies. Evaluate GPT-2 Small by argmax over the two candidates {IO, S}, with IO as the correct label; report exact agreement with the full model separately on its correct and error prompts. Use same-template ABC prompts for counterfactual resample ablation; evaluate mean and resample ablation. No general train/test split is specified for the main IOI evaluation. The separate error-recovery experiment evaluates on a frozen 26,000-example test set containing 225 full-model errors.

datasets.name: Docstring
datasets.eval_protocol: Use the public ACDC docstring benchmark to generate synthetic Python function signatures and partial docstrings; randomly sample argument names and description words from fixed vocabularies. Evaluate a four-layer attention-only transformer by argmax over 14 single-token candidates: the correct argument and 13 distractors. Generate counterfactual prompts using the generator's random_random corruption, which replaces argument names in both signature and docstring. Report exact model-circuit agreement separately on full-model correct and error prompts. No split is specified.

datasets.name: MIB: ARC-Easy
datasets.eval_protocol: Use published MIB prompts and dataset splits; evaluate the Llama-3.1 8B, Gemma-2 2b, and Qwen-2.5 0.5B settings. Circuits are extracted on the public-training split and evaluated on the public-test split. Use answer-letter options as candidates and report exact model-circuit agreement separately on full-model correct and error prompts. Use supplied symbol counterfactuals for ARC. Evaluate retained-edge fractions {0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1}, with an empty-circuit control.

datasets.name: MIB: ARC-Challenge
datasets.eval_protocol: Use published MIB prompts and dataset splits; evaluate the Llama-3.1 8B, Gemma-2 2b, and Qwen-2.5 0.5B settings. Circuits are extracted on the public-training split and evaluated on the public-test split. Use answer-letter options as candidates and report exact model-circuit agreement separately on full-model correct and error prompts. Use supplied symbol counterfactuals for ARC. Evaluate retained-edge fractions {0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1}, with an empty-circuit control.

datasets.name: MIB: arithmetic subtraction
datasets.eval_protocol: Use published MIB prompts and dataset splits, evaluating Llama-3.1 8B only because the other tested models tokenize numbers by digit and answers would fall outside the single-token candidate set. Circuits are extracted on the public-training split and evaluated on the public-test split. Candidates are single-token integers from 0 to 99; use random-operand counterfactuals and report exact model-circuit agreement separately on full-model correct and error prompts. Evaluate retained-edge fractions {0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1}, with an empty-circuit control.

baselines.name: Wang et al. IOI manual reference circuit
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on GPT-2 Small with the IOI candidate set and the same reported ablation settings and agreement measures as the other IOI circuits.

baselines.name: ACDC
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same task prompts, candidate-set argmax rule, and reported ablation settings as the other circuits. The IOI reference uses τ=0.003; Docstring uses τ=0.005 and τ=0.02.

baselines.name: EAP-IG-KL
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses KL divergence from the full model's output distribution as its discovery objective. The reported recovery circuit is the smallest evaluated non-full circuit meeting validation-resample faithfulness F_val ≥ 0.85; evaluated with the same task and ablation-specific agreement measures as the other circuits.

baselines.name: Edge Pruning
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on IOI using model-matching KL loss alongside sparsity. The reported circuit is the smallest evaluated non-full circuit meeting validation-resample faithfulness F_val ≥ 0.85; three fitted-seed sizes are listed and their agreement is averaged.

metrics.name: A_ok (correct agreement)
metrics.caveat: High agreement on model-correct prompts does not show that a circuit explains the model's failures; report A_err and Δ alongside it.

metrics.name: A_err (error agreement / exact error reproduction)
metrics.caveat: On full-model errors, agreement requires the circuit to return the same wrong answer; a correct answer or a different wrong answer is a disagreement. The paper additionally defines B_err to distinguish circuit errors from other disagreements.

metrics.name: Δ = A_ok − A_err
metrics.caveat: A smaller gap can result from improved error agreement or from reduced correct agreement; report A_ok and A_err separately.

metrics.name: Normalized task faithfulness F (normalized mean logit difference)
metrics.caveat: An average faithfulness score can conceal disagreement on individual prompts, especially failure to reproduce full-model errors; report correct and error agreement separately.

metrics.name: B_err (fraction of full-model error prompts on which the circuit is also incorrect)
metrics.caveat: Being incorrect does not establish that the circuit reproduces the model's particular wrong answer; report A_err as well. For binary tasks, B_err equals A_err.

controls.name: Structurally matched random extensions
controls.detail: Compare the selected IOI extension against structurally matched random extensions of the reference circuit; their test error agreement ranges from 17.33% to 41.33% (median 29.33%).
controls.rules_out: That adding an extension with the matched structure, without selecting the paper's particular head-position additions, is enough to produce the observed error recovery.

controls.name: Scalar subject-bias control
controls.detail: Apply a scalar subject bias to the IOI reference circuit, fitted on validation correct cases to match the selected extension's correct agreement; on the test set it has 98.93% correct agreement and 20.44% exact error agreement.
controls.rules_out: That the extension's error recovery is explained simply by biasing logits toward the subject while maintaining the same correct agreement.

controls.name: Empty-circuit control
controls.detail: Use graph- and ablation-specific empty controls in normalized faithfulness calculations; the MIB circuit-size evaluations also report the empty circuit at s=0.
controls.rules_out: That the faithfulness comparison is explained by the ablation-specific empty-circuit reference rather than retained circuit computation.

controls.name: Object substitution with S-inhibition outputs held fixed
controls.detail: After object-word substitution (for example, replacing the object with “snack”), repeat the intervention while holding S-inhibition outputs at their pre-substitution values; 68 of the corrections produced by substitution disappear.
controls.rules_out: That the object-substitution effect on the answer is independent of the proposed S-inhibition route.

confounds.name: Errors are too rare in discovery for circuits to learn to reproduce them
confounds.detail: The paper considers whether poor error agreement follows from few errors in discovery. In MIB, public-training splits contain 187–849 errors, or 4.9–41.1% of discovery examples; a Gemma ARC-Challenge example has 430 errors among 1,119 examples. The paper also reweights existing IOI errors to 50% of discovery KL weight and uses a 500-error/500-correct discovery split.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The gap persists in settings with many discovery errors. Reweighting raises mean-ablation exact-error agreement from 9.3% to 37.0% but leaves a gap and reduces correct agreement from 98.7% to 91.0%; the 500/500 split yields 44.2% error agreement and 91.4% correct agreement.

confounds.name: Error prompts have smaller margins and are therefore more sensitive to circuit-logit differences
confounds.detail: The paper notes that full-model errors may be concentrated near decision boundaries, which could account for agreement gaps.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Match correct and error test examples on the absolute full-model margin between the top two candidate logits. Some gaps narrow, but positive gaps persist in all reported IOI and most Docstring configurations, and in some MIB settings.

confounds.name: A smaller agreement gap reflects lost correct behavior rather than improved error reproduction
confounds.detail: Ablation or calibration can lower correct agreement while making the gap appear smaller; the paper gives Docstring resampling and threshold calibration as examples.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report A_ok and A_err separately, rather than the gap alone. The paper shows Docstring resampling's smaller gap is mainly due to A_ok falling from 77.1% to 47.2%, and notes that more aggressive threshold calibration can narrow the gap by sacrificing correct performance.

confounds.name: The recovered errors come from generic subject-logit bias rather than the selected omitted computations
confounds.detail: A generic shift toward the subject could reproduce errors without recovering the proposed position-specific computations.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare the selected extension with a scalar subject-bias control fitted to match its correct agreement: the control reaches only 20.44% exact error agreement, versus 75.11% for the extension, at 98.93% correct agreement for both.

confounds.name: Circuit errors on model-error prompts are being mistaken for reproduction of the model's specific errors
confounds.detail: A circuit can be wrong on a full-model error while choosing a different wrong answer, or even the task-correct answer, rather than the model's actual choice.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Define A_err by exact agreement with the full model's answer on its error prompts; additionally define B_err to report how often the circuit is wrong on those prompts and distinguish that from exact error reproduction.

evidence_standards.name: Bootstrap uncertainty intervals
evidence_standards.detail: For the table intervals, use 10,000 paired stratified bootstrap resamples, retain sampling weights, and condition on fitted masks. MIB circuit-size plots report point-wise 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

evidence_standards.name: Fitted-seed reporting
evidence_standards.detail: For Edge Pruning, report three fitted-seed circuit sizes and average their agreement.

evidence_standards.name: Candidate-set argmax evaluation
evidence_standards.detail: Report results under ranked-choice argmax over each task's specified candidate set, not free generation; agreement is with the full model's selected candidate.

datasets.name: InterpBench
datasets.eval_protocol: The main evaluation uses the 16 main SIIT models trained on Tracr circuits; the paper also evaluates the simplified IOI model in the circuit-correctness evaluation. For RQ1/RQ2, node effects are averaged over a test dataset, with plots for 7 randomly sampled tasks; normalized KL divergence is evaluated on 5 randomly sampled categorical tasks. Circuit-discovery methods are evaluated on the 16 main models using edge-level ROC AUC. Test-set sizes and episode counts are not specified.

baselines.name: IIT-trained transformers
baselines.fair_comparison: Trained with the same setup as SIIT models, except Weight_SIIT is set to 0.

baselines.name: Tracr-generated transformers
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with SIIT models on corresponding tasks/circuits; the paper uses Tracr as the high-level reference model.

baselines.name: Naturally trained supervised transformers
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with SIIT and Tracr transformers on corresponding tasks; the paper compares accuracy after ACDC-based mean ablation and weight distributions.

baselines.name: ACDC
baselines.fair_comparison: Circuit-discovery methods are evaluated on the same 16 SIIT models with edge-level ROC AUC; ACDC’s ROC AUC is obtained by varying its threshold.

baselines.name: Subnetwork Probing (node SP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same 16 SIIT models and compared using edge-level ROC AUC; SP’s ROC AUC is obtained by varying the regularization coefficient, with 3000 epochs.

baselines.name: Edgewise SP
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same 16 SIIT models and compared using edge-level ROC AUC; its masks are applied over edges rather than nodes.

baselines.name: Edge Attribution Patching (EAP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same 16 SIIT models and compared using edge-level ROC AUC.

baselines.name: EAP with integrated gradients (EAP-ig)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same 16 SIIT models and compared using edge-level ROC AUC; it uses 10 samples.

metrics.name: Node effect
metrics.caveat: For regression tasks, an intervention counts as having an effect only when the scalar output changes by at least 0.05.

metrics.name: Normalized KL divergence
metrics.caveat: SIIT need not match Tracr’s KL behavior exactly because Tracr fixes weights to output expected labels rather than minimizing cross-entropy; the authors attribute higher cross-case error bars to optimizing accuracy rather than matching the expected output distribution.

metrics.name: Accuracy after mean-ablating nodes rejected by ACDC
Correlation coefficient with naturally trained models

controls.name: IIT training with the SIIT loss removed
controls.detail: The same training setup is used, but Weight_SIIT is set to 0.
controls.rules_out: That the observed reduction in effects from non-circuit nodes follows merely from the shared training setup, rather than from adding SIIT’s strictness loss.

controls.name: Tracr-generated transformers
controls.detail: The corresponding Tracr model is used as a reference for circuit effects and outputs.
controls.rules_out: That SIIT’s circuit-effect pattern is being judged without comparison to the known circuit implementation.

controls.name: Mean and zero ablations
controls.detail: The authors repeat the node-effect experiments using mean and zero ablations in addition to interchange interventions.
controls.rules_out: Whether the circuit conclusions depend on the ablation type; mean ablations preserve separation of circuit and non-circuit nodes, while zero ablations do not.

controls.name: Naturally trained supervised transformers
controls.detail: For the realism evaluation, SIIT and Tracr models are compared with supervised models on corresponding tasks, using ACDC-rejected-node mean ablation and weight distributions.
controls.rules_out: That SIIT’s apparent realism is assessed only against the less realistic Tracr models.

confounds.name: Non-circuit nodes may perform part of the task, making apparent circuit consistency misleading
confounds.detail: A model can have perfect task accuracy and aligned-node consistency while non-aligned nodes still affect its output.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure node effects and normalized KL divergence after intervening on each node; SIIT models show low effects for non-circuit nodes and separation between circuit and non-circuit nodes.

confounds.name: The circuit conclusions may depend on the ablation method
confounds.detail: The benchmark is trained with interchange interventions, so results under that intervention alone might not establish robustness of the circuit claims.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Repeat the experiments with mean and zero ablations. Mean ablations retain separation, but zero ablations do not; the authors note this may indicate the circuits are not entirely true and that zero ablation may be unreliable.

confounds.name: Weak gradients, rather than an intrinsic weakness of gradient-based discovery methods, may explain poor SP and regular EAP results
confounds.detail: The authors observe very small gradients in SIIT models, possibly because training reaches 100% IIA and SIIA; this could account for the methods’ poor performance.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The authors manually inspect gradients and find them very small. This supports the alternative explanation rather than ruling it out.

confounds.name: Results on these models may not generalize to larger, more functional models
confounds.detail: The authors concede that InterpBench models are very small and implement only one algorithmic circuit, unlike larger models with many subtasks.
confounds.ruled_out_by: No measurement in this evaluation rules out this limitation; the authors state that results may not accurately represent larger models.

evidence_standards.name: Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney U-test with Vargha–Delaney A12 effect size
evidence_standards.detail: For circuit-discovery comparisons, the paper treats p < 0.05 as statistically significant and reports A12 effect sizes. It reports p ≈ 0.0004 for ACDC versus SP and p ≥ 0.05 for ACDC versus EAP-ig; the latter is described as statistically indistinguishable.

datasets.name: IOI (Indirect Object Identification)
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses 15 sentence templates with clean ABBA/BABA prompts; measures recovered logit difference between the correct name A and incorrect name B. The paper uses an ABC corrupt distribution with independently sampled names for resampling and mean ablation; its Figure 3 uses 100 ABC prompts for these ablations. It also varies the ABC dataset size used to compute mean activations.

datasets.name: Tracr Reverse
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluates automatic circuit-discovery methods by sweeping importance thresholds and plotting pessimistic ROC curves against ground-truth circuits under the relevant ablation methodology; compares area under the curves.

datasets.name: Tracr X-Proportion
datasets.eval_protocol: Task outputs, at each token, the proportion of previous characters that are x’s. Evaluates automatic circuit-discovery methods by sweeping importance thresholds and plotting pessimistic ROC curves against ground-truth circuits under Zero and Resample Ablations; compares area under the curves.

baselines.name: ACDC
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with Subnetwork Probing and Head Importance Scoring on the same Tracr tasks, using importance-threshold sweeps and ROC curves. ACDC uses edge ablations; the paper adjusts Subnetwork Probing and Head Importance Scoring to use or approximate edge ablations for the comparison.

baselines.name: Subnetwork Probing (SP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with ACDC and Head Importance Scoring on the same Tracr tasks, using importance-threshold sweeps and ROC curves. The paper adjusts SP to learn masks that ablate edges, matching the edge-based evaluation used by ACDC.

baselines.name: Head Importance Scoring (HISP)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with ACDC and Subnetwork Probing on the same Tracr tasks, using importance-threshold sweeps and ROC curves. The paper adjusts HISP to assign attribution scores by approximating edge patching, matching the edge-based evaluation used by ACDC.

metrics.name: Logit difference recovered
metrics.caveat: Scores vary with prompt format and individual examples; the paper reports ABBA and BABA results separately and shows the per-prompt distribution, including IQRs up to 50% and extreme outliers.
